summary:
Here is my complete analysis of `customerCode` and everything derived from it in this Spring PetClinic REST repository.

## 1. Where `customerCode` is generated (format logic)

**File:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`

The `customerCode` is assigned during `addOwner(...)` (line 126) and computed by the private helper `nextCustomerCode(String lastName)`:

```java
233	    /**
234	     * Builds the customer code for a new owner, formatted {@code '<LAST3>-<NNNN>'} where LAST3 is the
235	     * upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN is a global 4-digit zero-padded
236	     * sequence equal to one more than the current number of owners (e.g. {@code 'SMI-0007'}).
237	     ...
241	    private String nextCustomerCode(String lastName) {
242	        String prefix = lastName.substring(0, Math.min(3, lastName.length())).toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
243	        int sequence = this.clinicService.findAllOwners().size() + 1;
244	        return String.format("%s-%04d", prefix, sequence);
245	    }
```

Current format: `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` (e.g. `SMI-0007`). LAST3 = upper-cased first 3 chars of last name; NNNN = (total owner count + 1), zero-padded to 4 digits.

Call site (line 126):
```java
126	        owner.setCustomerCode(nextCustomerCode(owner.getLastName()));
```

Note: `city` is NOT currently used in the code — but the acceptance test (see section 5) expects a `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` format, so this logic is out of sync with the intended spec.

## 2. Everything derived from `customerCode`

**a) Membership number** — same file, `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`, assigned at line 127, built by `membershipNumber(...)`:

```java
247	    /**
248	     * Builds the membership number for a new owner, formatted {@code '<customerCode>-M<YY>'} where YY is
249	     * the last two digits of the registration date's year (e.g. {@code 'SMI-0007-M26'}).
250	     ...
255	    private String membershipNumber(String customerCode, LocalDate registrationDate) {
256	        String yy = String.format("%02d", registrationDate.getYear() % 100);
257	        return String.format("%s-M%s", customerCode, yy);
258	    }
```

Call site (line 127):
```java
127	        owner.setMembershipNumber(membershipNumber(owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate()));
```

Format: `<customerCode>-M<YY>` (e.g. `SMI-0007-M26`), where YY = last two digits of the registration year.

**b) Membership tier** — NOT derived from customerCode, but a related derived value. In `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java` (lines 26-38), `membershipTier` is computed from `namesakeCount` and `email`:
```java
34	    default String toMembershipTier(Owner owner) {
35	        boolean hasEmail = owner.getEmail() != null && !owner.getEmail().isEmpty();
36	        boolean noNamesakes = owner.getNamesakeCount() != null && owner.getNamesakeCount() == 0;
37	        return noNamesakes && hasEmail ? "SILVER" : "BRONZE";
38	    }
```

`namesakeCount` is set at line 128 of the controller via `countNamesakes(firstName, lastName)` (lines 269-278) — counts existing owners sharing first+last name (case-insensitive) by iterating `findAllOwners()`.

## 3. Owner / Customer entity definition

**File:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` (`@Entity`, `@Table(name = "owners")`, extends `Person`). Fields:

- line 40 `address` (`@NotEmpty`)
- line 44 `city` (`@NotEmpty`)
- line 49 `telephone` (`@Pattern` E.164)
- line 52 `email`
- line 55 `registrationDate` (LocalDate)
- line 58 `customerCode` (`@Column(name = "customer_code")`)
- line 61 `membershipNumber` (`@Column(name = "membership_number")`)
- line 64 `householdId`
- line 67 `namesakeCount` (Integer)
- line 70 `pets` (OneToMany)

Getters/setters for `customerCode` at lines 112-118; for `membershipNumber` at lines 120-126.

**Base class:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Person.java` (`@MappedSuperclass`, extends `BaseEntity`) — line 33 `firstName`, line 37 `lastName` (both `@NotEmpty`), getters/setters lines 39-53.

## 4. Service/repository methods for counting/querying owners by city

There is NO dedicated "count owners by city" or "query by city" method in the codebase currently. Relevant findings:

- **`OwnerRepository`** (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/OwnerRepository.java`) exposes only: `findByLastName(String)` (line 46), `findByLastName(String, Pageable)` (line 48), `findById(int)` (line 57), `save(Owner)` (line 66), `findAll()` (line 74), `findAll(Pageable)` (line 76), `delete(Owner)` (line 84). No city-based query.
- **`ClinicService`** (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicService.java`): `findAllOwners()` (line 57), `isHouseholdInUse(lastName, address, excludeId)` (line 62), `assignHousehold(Owner)` (line 63). Implemented in `ClinicServiceImpl.java` (lines 131, 251, 265). No city count method.
- All count-style logic (sequence for customerCode, namesakes, telephone-in-use) is done in-memory in the controller by iterating `clinicService.findAllOwners()` (controller lines 243, 271, 403). So counting owners by city would today require iterating `findAllOwners()` and filtering on `getCity()` — no such method exists yet.
- The JDBC SQL in `JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl.java` selects `city` but never filters/counts by it (lines 86, 101, 125, 160, 186, 201).

## 5. Existing tests referencing customerCode / membership / derived values

**File:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java` (full file, 16 lines):

```java
7	/** customer-code-city: Change the customerCode format to '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where CITY3 is the upper-cased... */
8	class AcceptanceTest extends AcceptanceBase {
10		@Test
11		void coreCustomerCodeHasCityPrefix() throws Exception {
12			int id = createOwnerOk(ownerNode());
13			JsonNode n = fetchOwner(id);
14			assertTrue(n.get("customerCode").asText().matches("[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\\d{4}")); // <CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>
15		}
16	}
```

This test expects the format `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}` (i.e. `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`), which the current `nextCustomerCode` (section 1) does NOT produce — it produces `<LAST3>-<NNNN>`. The test will currently fail; the intended change is to prepend a city prefix.

**File:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java` — the abstract base (322 lines) providing the harness. Relevant to membership/city/derived rules:
- Class-level docs (lines 37-41) mention "membership number, per-day cap, per-city cap, 'most common city'" rules and `@Transactional` rollback isolation.
- Annotations (lines 47-50): `@SpringBootTest`, `@AutoConfigureMockMvc`, `@Transactional`, `@WithMockUser(roles = {"OWNER_ADMIN","VET_ADMIN","ADMIN"})`.
- `ownerNode()` (lines 117-125) builds a valid unique owner with a unique `city` via `uniqueCity()` (lines 94-96, `"Town"+seq()`).
- `fillCity(String city, int n)` (lines 173-179) creates n owners in the same city — for per-city cap rules.
- Helpers: `createOwnerOk` (line 160), `fetchOwner` (line 200), `knownOwner(city)` (line 260).
- Pinned reference data: `CITY_REGION`, `REGION_TIMEZONE`, `REGION_POSTCODES` (lines 228-237), plus `sha256hex`/`shaHex`/`luhn` derived-value helpers (lines 282-321). These support other derived-value rules but are not yet used by the single active test.

No other test files reference `customerCode` or `membershipNumber`.

## 6. Build tool and running tests

- **Build tool:** Maven, with the Maven Wrapper present. POM at `/home/daniel/sandbox/pom.xml` (`artifactId` = `spring-petclinic-rest`, parent `spring-boot-starter-parent`). Wrapper script `/home/daniel/sandbox/mvnw` (executable) and `mvnw.cmd`. Test deps include `spring-boot-starter-test`, `spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test`, `spring-boot-starter-security-test`, `mockito-core`.
- **Run the full test suite:**
  - `./mvnw test` (from `/home/daniel/sandbox`)
  - Run just the acceptance test: `./mvnw test -Dtest=AcceptanceTest`
  - Full build with tests: `./mvnw clean install` (README line 218 references `mvn clean install`).

### Summary of the customerCode flow
`addOwner` → `nextCustomerCode(lastName)` builds `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` (count-based sequence) → stored on `Owner.customerCode` → `membershipNumber(customerCode, registrationDate)` derives `<customerCode>-M<YY>` → stored on `Owner.membershipNumber`. The acceptance test expects a city-prefixed `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` format that the current code does not yet implement, and there is no existing per-city count method to draw the CITY3 prefix or any city-cap logic from.
